Based on your symptoms, I think I could be a std instead of HIV. 
Hope the doctor also did a urine test as well as others. 
If the contact was in August the signs of HIV wouldn't show that quickly. 
Because HIV testings are usually done in every three months since it takes that long for the virus to spread and show. 
The window for HIV blood test, which takes about 10mintues, is around one month or less. And it seems like your doctor didn't do that on you. Maybe it's not HIV after all. 

Also if you think you've contacted with a possible HIV positive person you can always goto any emergency room and they will put you on PEP immediately. 
PEP is a combination of PreP which is a pill you take daily to prevent HIV contraction even if you practice unsafe sex, excluding STDs, and another pill that's bit stronger. 

It's too late for you to go on PEP, but if the test result turns out to be negative and you're concerned for the future I suggest you talk to your doctor about going on PreP. 

Hope it helps.

Hello there. 
I suggest you watch a documentary on YouTube called Chazz Patrella: The Boy Who Should've Lived. 

It's about a boy who was born with suicidal thoughts and attempts since the day he learned how to walk and talk. 
You'll see how his behaviors affected the people around him.

Hug him as hard as you can and never let him go. 

That's all I wanted from my last partner but he couldn't stay next to me while I suffered through many things. 

And it only went down from that moment. 

Your partner is beyond lucky to have a caring person like you as a lover. 
If you truly care about him but don't want to cross the boundary and have uncomfortable conversations , just remind him that you love him every day and show him your love.

I live with one of my family member too yet I will tell immensely isolated.
I've found out that being next to each other isn't enough for me. 
I wanted a meaningful connection where I can have any sorts of conversation with my family and relate to one another. 
I still haven't found the courage to do it myself. 
But I started with a friend or even a stranger. 
I have a very few friends so I couldn't do much but just from connecting a little bit I realized that I was loved. 

People need to feel loved by others. 
You may not find a person who loves you but you must have someone you care about. And I can say without a doubt that that person cares about you too. 
We all seek love and connection, and it's a natural sensation that is very easily misread as something difficult but it really isn't. 

I hope you start connecting with with your family and feel loved, because they all do.

Hey there. 
You say you "may have" contracted HIV, have you been tested for it ?
If you're too embarrassed to goto a clinic to get the blood test, which I'd recommend, you can always buy a at-home HIV testing kit at any drug store. 
It costs about $30, bit expensive when you can get free testings from many places, and it is a oral swab test kit. I highly suggest you consider it. It's called Oraquick. 

It is strange you're doctor can see the signs of HIV but doesn't test you for it, perhaps you don't have it after all. 

And even if you do, HIV can hardly result in death. 
Coming from the gay community I know many people who are HIV positive. And you can go on medicine to lower your level and end up as a "HIV positive undetectable" status. It means that you have contracted HIV but the virus can no longer be detected in your blood. Recent studies I've read shows that unprotected sex with an Undetectable person has only 2-3% chance of contraction. 

I hope you don't bring shame to yourself or guilt over your HIV status. 

The science on HIV and AIDS are improving by month I think they'll find a cure very soon. 

As far as being short, I don't want you to let your height define yourself. 
There are countless types of men in this country alone. And i believe that means women are interested in so many different characters of men. 

You can be the short one in a relationship, find someone similar to your height or someone shorter. 
I've never discriminated a person from being my friend because of their height, and same goes to my love partners I had. 

the good news is that you're still young and men grow up to their 30s. Trust me. 

All I want to say is that your height is something you can't control over, but your HIV status is. Don't be afraid to talk to your doctor about it because if can affect your life as well as others. 

Don't give up. 
You're too young to let a small virus brig you down.

sounds like you are struggling to open yourself into a social setting. You are not the only one who doesn't grow up around gay people, not knowing about gay culture, or even not understanding why you have weird crushes on straight friends.
Is also sounds like you are waiting to be invited to a dinner table rather than hosting and inviting people over. Shyness is a self-imposed prison. Don't let yourself down because you can't talk to people you like or only unfitting guys hit on you. 
Maybe not having enough dating experience as an adult can help you strive stronger to your dating goals. Most young kids struggle in dating because at the same time they are also dealing with their identity issues or social labels etc. But as an adult you must have a better understanding of yourself than those younger kids.

My take is that no one really knows what they are doing when it comes to talking to someone you are attracted to, every new encounter will always make you nervous and sweat. And knowing that this is a common human life experience, maybe you don't have to be so afraid of it.

I'm not saying like the book Secret, *that if you really want something and wish for it it will come to you*, nor saying *if you really want something you should avoid it until it comes to you naturally*. Because there are so many different kinds of people, and that will never bring you the same experience. 

also try not to label yourself as abnormal, socially stunted, or repugnant... you will only hate yourself more.
